title: A Post-Registration Checklist for New Businesses in Nepal (30-Day Rules)
metaDescription: Essential 30-day compliance checklist after receiving your OCR incorporation certificate in Nepal. Ward registration, PAN/VAT, bank account, and share lagat.
h1: A Post-Registration Checklist for New Businesses
directAnswer: After receiving your Certificate of Incorporation from the Office of Company Registrar (OCR), you must complete four mandatory statutory steps within 30 days: register your business with the local Municipal Ward Office, obtain a corporate PAN/VAT certificate from the Inland Revenue Department (IRD), open a corporate bank account and deposit share capital, and submit formal Share Allotment records (Share Lagat) to the OCR.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.h2: The 4 Critical Statutory Milestones Within 30 Days
sections.contentHtml:
Many founders mistakenly assume incorporation ends at the OCR. Neglecting post-registration mandates attracts statutory penalties and operational paralysis:

1. Municipal Ward Business Permitting (Within 30 Days)

Under the Local Government Operation Act 2074, businesses must register with the Ward Office where their physical office is located and pay municipal business tax and signboard fees.

2. Inland Revenue Department (PAN / VAT Registration)

Submit your company incorporation certificate, Ward registration, and lease agreement to the local IRO to obtain your corporate PAN certificate.

3. Corporate Bank Account Opening & Share Capital Inflow

Adopt a board resolution, complete bank KYC, and require all promoters to deposit their committed share equity into the corporate account.

4. Filing Share Allotment (Share Lagat) at OCR

Submit bank balance certificates proving capital deposit to the OCR and obtain the official OCR Share Lagat Certificate (फाँटवारी).

sections.h2: Fines for Delayed Share Lagat Submission
sections.contentHtml: Failing to file Share Lagat at the OCR within the statutory timeline incurs escalating monthly fines under Section 81 of the Companies Act 2063. Explore our post-incorporation compliance management retainers.

faqs.question: Can our company issue commercial invoices before obtaining a PAN?
faqs.answer: No. Under the Income Tax Act 2058, conducting commercial sales or issuing invoices without a registered PAN is strictly illegal and attracts severe seizure penalties.
